notes:
Acts is Luke writing, so almost everything here is `scripture` — but this build is
the exception the law names: the speaker in Acts 1:7-8 is the RISEN CHRIST, talking
to the eleven on the day he ascends. A red-letter King James Bible inks those verses.
So the one red beat STAYS red, and it grows:

  j1  Acts 1:8  RED -> RED (jesus), but rewritten to the full verbatim verse. The
      old line dropped 'both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria' out of
      the middle, which made it a paraphrase wearing Old English clothes. It is now
      exactly what a viewer finds in Acts 1:8.
  j0  Acts 1:7  NEW (jesus). n0 already told the viewer the disciples asked about
      restoring the kingdom; his actual answer was never on screen. It is now, in his
      own words, immediately before verse 8. Same still as j1 — two consecutive beats
      over ST2, no new artwork.

LIFTED FROM PARAPHRASE — the two men in white:
  s11 Acts 1:11  NEW (scripture, light blue). n3 said 'two figures in white stood
      beside them with a promise' and then n4 gave the promise in modern English,
      which meant the single most quotable line in the chapter never got spoken as
      scripture. s11 now says it verbatim and n4 retells it, unchanged, right after.
      These are angels/messengers, not Christ — light blue, not red and not green.
      s11 and n4 share ST7.

Nothing left as paraphrase from uncertainty. Acts 1:7, 1:8 and 1:11 are all quoted
in full from the King James text.

WHY-LAW: milk. He did not leave them staring at the sky. He left them a job, a
companion, and a promise to come back — and all three are on screen in the words
they were actually said in.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In his last moments with them, the disciples asked Jesus if he was going to restore the kingdom right then. He turned them toward something bigger.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That is not a no. It is a redirection. The timing belongs to the Father, he told them, and it is not yours to work out — but the power is yours, and so is the work. He was handing them the mission. Go tell everyone, everywhere, starting right where you're standing. And then something happened they would never forget.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they watched, he was lifted up,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and a cloud received him out of their sight. They stood there staring into the sky, stunned.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then two figures in white stood beside them with a promise:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This same Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come back the same way you've seen him go.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He did not abandon them. He left them a mission, a promise, and the sure word that he's coming again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He's coming back the same way he left. Until then, you're not alone — and you're not without purpose.

stills_wanted.ST2: ST2 now carries both halves of what he actually said — verse seven and verse eight, back to back, red the whole way. Frame the moment of the words: the risen Lord facing the eleven on the hillside, close enough to speak normally, his hands still visible. Not a farewell pose and not yet an ascent — he is giving instructions. Steady, unhurried, eye-level, so the viewer reads authority rather than drama.
stills_wanted.ST7: ST7 now holds the promise twice, once in the King James words and once retold — the colour goes light blue and then white over one image. Frame the two men in white apparel standing beside the disciples on the Mount of Olives, speaking to them, while the disciples are still turned upward. The messengers should read as sent, not glorious: plain white, no wings, no blaze. The emotional beat is reassurance interrupting a stare.
